# CodeSnap

CodeSnap is a tool for generating beautiful code snapshots (images or HTML) from code snippets. It provides a command-line tool and a library interface so you can generate snapshots directly or integrate snapshot generation into other programs.

Features
- Generate high-quality code snapshots with optional line numbers and watermarking.
- Multiple output formats (PNG, SVG, HTML, and more).
- Customizable themes, fonts, and backgrounds.
- Clipboard support for copying snapshot output.

Usage (CLI)

Generate a snapshot from a source file:

codesnap -f ./path/to/source.file -o ./output.png

See command help for available options:

codesnap -h

Configuration

CodeSnap accepts configuration in JSON format to control theme, window appearance, font choices, watermark, background, and other visual options. Supply a configuration to the CLI or use the library API to programmatically configure snapshot generation.

Examples

# Generate a PNG from a file
codesnap -f ./example.py -o ./snapshot.png

# Output HTML
codesnap -f ./example.js -o ./snapshot.html

item.text:
Implemented a clean-room reimplementation in [codesnap.py](/workspace/codesnap.py) with [compile.sh](/workspace/compile.sh) installing it as `./executable`. It recreates the observed CLI surface, default config generation, PNG/SVG output, gradient/window snapshot rendering, execution mode, range handling, line numbers, breadcrumbs, title, add/delete/highlight bands, ASCII warning behavior, and the headless clipboard failure path.

Verified in this environment with `./executable --version`, `-c`, `-f`, `--silent`, `--type ascii`, `-e ... --skip`, and clipboard/error cases, plus a final smoke test generating `/workspace/final_smoke.png`. Residual risk is in the less common flags I didn’t re-check exhaustively after switching the final build to the dependency-free Python implementation.
